rounds.proof_sketch: input.size(2) = 64, input.size(3) = 64 in fixed shape [16, 32, 64, 64, 64]. Mutation reads wrong dimension but gets same value. All downstream: output_height, ih_end bounds, depth_offset calculations use input_height=64 identically.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation substitutes input.size(3) with input.size(2) when computing input_height. However, the fixed input shape [16, 32, 64, 64, 64] has depth=64 and height=64, meaning both dimension lookups return identical values. The computed input_height=64 is then used consistently throughout the kernel for output dimension calculation, loop bounds, and index arithmetic. Since the numeric value is the same, all memory accesses, averaging operations, and output writes are identical. This is a latent bug that would only manifest with non-square spatial dimensions.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. The mutation reads the wrong tensor dimension for height, but dimensions 2 and 3 coincidentally equal 64. Killing requires an input shape where depth ≠ height (e.g., [16, 32, 32, 64, 64]), which violates the fixed-shape testing constraint.
rounds.recommendations: Include test configurations with non-uniform spatial dimensions (e.g., depth ≠ height ≠ width) to catch dimension-indexing bugs. The symmetric shape [16, 32, 64, 64, 64] masks bugs where dimensions are confused.
